summary: add_key_rows wrote absent for every unseen expected registry value even when the enumeration that produced 'unseen' was itself incomplete -- an incomplete read cannot prove a value doesn't exist
trigger: a RegEnumValueW enumeration that fails partway through (cap, transient error) before covering every expected value name
classification_rationale: an unseen-due-to-incomplete-enumeration value is a different fact from a genuinely-absent one, and the binding absent-vs-failure contract requires they read differently

summary: the file header claimed only ci_policy.reg was REAL CAPTURE and everything else RECONSTRUCTION, but secureboot_state.reg and deviceguard_real.reg are also real captures per their own .provenance.txt, and ci_policy.reg is a disclosed hybrid (real values, reconstructed reg export serialisation) -- flagged independently by Gate 3 quality-engineer and Gate 4 consistency-auditor
trigger: a reader taking the header comment as the test's actual evidentiary basis
classification_rationale: a comment-accuracy defect only -- doesn't change what the tests assert or their pass/fail outcome

summary: the enumeration-completeness fix's pathological branch (incomplete enumeration -> unreadable) is directly tested, but its realistic HAPPY branch -- a COMPLETE enumeration where an expected value is legitimately absent (e.g. any pre-Windows-11-22H2 host without Smart App Control) -- is not exercised by any test or real-hardware capture
trigger: reviewing test coverage for the common real-world case rather than the edge case
classification_rationale: the fixed code path's happy-path branch is unproven, not shown broken -- a coverage gap on the more common real-world shape

summary: read_value()'s dword/text branches don't re-validate the second RegQueryValueExW call's own returned type/size against the first probe's plan -- a narrow TOCTOU window where a changed-type value could be silently misread with no failure token
trigger: an actor with write access to the SYSTEM-protected registry keys involved, changing a value's type between the size-probe and fill calls
classification_rationale: corrected: the actor doesn't escalate privilege via this bug (E2 doesn't apply) -- they already hold write access to the SYSTEM-protected key as a PRECONDITION, which is what makes this a race (E5), not an escalation. I3+E5 derives HIGH/BLOCKING. Fixed: read_value() now re-checks the fill call's own returned type against the probed type on both the dword and text paths, failing closed (unreadable, type_changed) on a mismatch rather than trusting stale plan state.

summary: the Linux EFBIG (oversized-file) branch has no test reaching it -- architecturally hard to trigger under the pure-core/thin-shell split
trigger: an efivars/securityfs file exceeding the plugin's read bound
classification_rationale: low real-world likelihood, the branch itself reads correctly on inspection, just unexercised by any test
